question: Before a 9 year old boy with testicular pain of 6 hours of evolution, intense, that almost prevents him from walking, without previous trauma, what is the most probable diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Testicular pain -> 6 hours of evolution -> intense -> difficulty walking -> no previous trauma -> 90% CHAIN: Testicular pain -> intense -> difficulty walking -> no previous trauma -> testicular torsion -> 80% CHAIN: Testicular pain -> intense -> difficulty walking -> no previous trauma -> epididymitis -> 10% CHAIN: Testicular pain -> intense -> difficulty walking -> no previous trauma -> crural hernia -> 90%
analysis: Given the sudden onset of intense testicular pain in a 9-year-old boy without trauma, the most probable diagnosis would be testicular torsion. Testicular torsion is a medical emergency that requires immediate intervention to prevent loss of blood flow to the testicle.
